title: Rain-Wrapped
subtitle: Night Tornado Warning & Shelter Timing

brief.userPrompt: A Friday night in mid-December, unusually warm and humid. At 15:00 the Storm Prediction Center's Day 1 outlook places Brennan County in a Moderate (4) risk with significant tornadoes possible after dark; NWS Paducah's afternoon briefing warns of a fast-moving line with embedded tornadoes between 22:00 and 02:00. At 20:15 a tornado watch (PDS) is issued until 04:00. The exercise starts at 21:30 with the BCEMA EOC at Level 2 (EM Director Dana Whitfield, Warning Officer, PIO Caleb Harmon) and Channel 6 StormTeam's Chief Meteorologist Marisa Kent on air. Pressure points: when to open the Ashford Middle School and Corwin Community Center safe rooms (20 and 15 minutes to unlock at night) and how to tell people in the Clarks River manufactured home parks to move before warnings; the North zone sirens N-07 (Pine Hollow) and N-11 (Clarks River bridge) are out of service; at 22:41 NWS Paducah issues a tornado warning (RADAR INDICATED, CONSIDERABLE) for northern Brennan County moving northeast at 60 mph, followed by an upgrade to OBSERVED after a spotter report near Corwin and later a tornado emergency for Corwin; the overnight shifts at Ridgeline Distribution (310 workers) and Corwin Wax & Candle (95) must shelter; BrennanAlert voice calls take 12 minutes to complete; a viral post claims the Corwin safe room is locked; Channel 6 loses its studio power and goes to the basement backup set; cell towers fail on battery after midnight; 911 receives entrapment calls at the candle plant and the Pine Hollow park; damage assessment, the Red Cross shelter at Brennan County High School, requests to Kentucky Emergency Management, and coordination with NWS Paducah's storm survey. The broadcast meteorologist never contradicts an NWS warning; the county never duplicates an NWS tornado warning by WEA.
audience: Channel 6 StormTeam (Broadcast Meteorologist and News Director)
constraints: Every email address of the county uses the exercise domain brennancoky.example; Channel 6 uses channel6stormteam.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

NWS products (tornado warnings, severe weather statements, the tornado emergency) follow the real NWS format and impact-based tags, and are marked as exercise products; times are Central Standard Time.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; NWS Paducah, Kentucky Emergency Management, neighboring counties, the Red Cross, the employers, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Acting before the warning, waking people who are asleep, and keeping county and broadcast messages the same as each power source, siren and cell tower fails.
overview.threat: On an unusually warm, humid Friday night in mid-December, a fast-moving line of storms with tornadoes embedded in it crosses Brennan County. Before STARTEX, the Storm Prediction Center's 15:00 CST Day 1 outlook put the county in a Moderate (4) risk with significant tornadoes possible after dark. NWS Paducah's afternoon briefing warned of embedded tornadoes between 22:00 and 02:00, and at 20:15 a Particularly Dangerous Situation (PDS) tornado watch was issued until 04:00. At 22:41, NWS Paducah issues a tornado warning (RADAR INDICATED, CONSIDERABLE) for northern Brennan County, with the storm moving northeast at 60 mph. A spotter report near Corwin brings an upgrade to OBSERVED, and NWS Paducah later issues a tornado emergency for Corwin. The storms hit outdoor sirens (North zone sirens N-07 and N-11 are already out of service), BrennanAlert, Channel 6 StormTeam's studio, cell towers and the overnight 911 floor.
overview.operationalImpact:
At 21:30 CST, the BCEMA EOC is at Level 2 with EM Director Dana Whitfield, the Warning Officer and PIO Caleb Harmon. Channel 6 StormTeam's Chief Meteorologist Marisa Kent is on air. Neither safe room is open. The Ashford Middle School safe room takes 20 minutes to unlock at night and the Corwin Community Center 15 minutes, so the opening decision has to come well before the line arrives. About 1,100 residents of the Clarks River manufactured home parks (Pine Hollow, Riverbend, Shady Acres) must be told to move to a sturdy building before any warning. Only Pine Hollow has a shelter, and it holds 60. The Pine Hollow siren (N-07) and the Clarks River bridge siren (N-11) will not sound.

When the 22:41 warning comes, 911 must activate the sirens in the zones inside the polygon within one minute. The Warning Officer sends BrennanAlert, but the voice calls take 12 minutes to finish against a storm moving at 60 mph. The county must not send its own WEA that repeats the NWS tornado warning. Ridgeline Distribution (310 workers on the overnight shift) and Corwin Wax & Candle (95 workers, no refuge area on the production floor) call to ask whether to shelter. A viral post claims the Corwin safe room is locked. Channel 6 loses studio power and moves to its basement backup set, and its meteorologist must stay consistent with the NWS warning while checking the rumor with the county.

After midnight, cell towers running on battery start to fail, which cuts off WEA, BrennanAlert and the spotter relay for parts of the county. The overnight 911 floor has two telecommunicators and one supervisor. It takes entrapment calls from the candle plant and the Pine Hollow park while fire and sheriff crews work in debris and darkness. Later, the EOC moves to full activation and must handle damage assessment, the Red Cross shelter request for Brennan County High School, resource requests to Kentucky Emergency Management, and support for NWS Paducah's storm survey.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to decide, ahead of any NWS Paducah tornado warning, to unlock the Ashford Middle School (20 minutes) and Corwin Community Center (15 minutes) safe rooms and to tell the roughly 1,100 residents of the Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres manufactured home parks to move to a sturdy building, while the PDS tornado watch is in effect and the line is coming at 60 mph.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to carry out BWN 3 and the Level 3 triggers in EOP 3.1 when the 22:41 tornado warning arrives: sound the North zone sirens inside the polygon from Position 2 within one minute, log and work around failed sirens N-07 and N-11, and send BrennanAlert without sending a county WEA that repeats the NWS tornado warning.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep the county's public messages and Channel 6 StormTeam's coverage from its basement backup set matched to the NWS warning, the OBSERVED upgrade and the Corwin tornado emergency, and to check and correct the viral claim that the Corwin safe room is locked through the Warning Officer–broadcast contact named in CSSWCP 4.

objectives.name: Operational Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to prioritize and dispatch to entrapment calls at Corwin Wax & Candle and the Pine Hollow park with two telecommunicators and one supervisor as battery-powered cell towers fail, and then to move to full EOC activation for damage assessment, the Red Cross shelter request for Brennan County High School, the Kentucky Emergency Management resource requests and access for the NWS Paducah storm survey.

roles.name: EM Director (EOC Command)
roles.team: Team A: EM Director / EOC Command
roles.description: Owns EOC activation level, the safe room opening decision, any countywide siren activation outside NWS warnings, and requests for state assistance through the KYEM Area 1 Manager.
standingOrders: Lead Time First: open the safe rooms on the forecast and the watch, not on the warning. The unlock times leave no room to wait for a polygon.
Escalate Early: move to Level 3 per EOP 3.1 the moment a warning, a confirmed tornado or damage reports reach the county, and call KYEM before you are sure you need them.
One Voice: coordinate with NWS Paducah, Ashford and Corwin before you announce anything. Do not let the county issue its own forecast.
Own the Gaps: when a siren, tower or alert channel fails, assign someone to reach the people it covered.

roles.name: Warning Officer
roles.description: Manages NWS product monitoring, siren activation confirmation, BrennanAlert and county WEA messages, and the warning log for the county.
standingOrders: Follow the Product: base every alert on what NWS Paducah issued (places, times, tag) and never send a county WEA that repeats the NWS tornado warning.
Speed over Polish: send the BrennanAlert as soon as the warning drops. The voice calls need 12 minutes to finish, and the storm moves a mile a minute.
Log Everything: record each activation, each failed siren (N-07, N-11) and each channel that goes down, with the time.
Broadcast Contact: you are Channel 6's named Brennan County contact. Confirm or deny rumors to them quickly, but only with facts you have checked.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns the county's public messages, coordination with Channel 6 StormTeam and other media, and rumor monitoring on social media.
standingOrders: Truth over Reassurance: if a safe room is not yet open, say so and say when it will be. Do not deny a rumor you have not checked.
Match the Warning: every county post uses the NWS warning's places, times and tag and adds only county actions such as shelter openings.
Kill Rumors at the Source: confirm the safe room status with the EOC, then correct it on every channel and with Channel 6 in a single message.
Keep the Clock: after the storm, issue a joint county, Ashford and Corwin message at least every two hours per EOP 3.4.

roles.name: Brennan County Communications (911) Supervisor
roles.description: Manages the overnight 911 floor, siren activation from Position 2, spotter-triggered siren decisions and the triage of damage, injury and entrapment calls.
standingOrders: Do Not Wait: sound the zones inside the polygon within one minute per BWN 3. If a trained spotter or law enforcement reports a tornado before any warning, sound that zone and the zone downstream.
Triage Ruthlessly: with two telecommunicators, entrapments and life threats come before damage-only calls. Log the rest in CAD for damage assessment.
Report Failures: tell the Warning Officer right away about every siren that fails its polling check and every loss of tower or radio.
Protect the Floor: ask the EOC for call-taking help before the queue overwhelms the console.

roles.name: Field Incident Commander (Fire / Sheriff Field Operations)
roles.team: Team E: Fire / Sheriff Field Operations
roles.description: Manages field response, search and rescue, and scene security by the fire districts and the Sheriff's Office under NIMS incident command.
standingOrders: Safety First: if the screen and the field disagree, trust the field. Hold crews while a tornado warning still covers their area.
Rescue Before Assessment: put fire districts on the Corwin Wax & Candle and Pine Hollow entrapments before you survey damage.
Report Up: send spotter-quality tornado and damage reports to 911 and the EOC so they reach NWS Paducah, even when cell coverage drops.
Secure and Preserve: secure damage scenes and keep access open for the road department and the NWS storm survey team.

roles.name: Broadcast Meteorologist on Duty (Channel 6 StormTeam)
roles.description: Owns Channel 6 StormTeam's wall-to-wall and tornado emergency coverage, the move to the basement backup set, and on-air consistency with NWS warnings and county messages.
standingOrders: Lead with the Warning: give the NWS places, times, tag and action first. Present storm-track arrival times as estimates.
Verify Before Airing: air no unconfirmed reports of locked shelters, damage or casualties. Check with the Brennan County Warning Officer and name the source.
Stay on Air: keep coverage going from the backup set until no tornado warning remains. Tell manufactured home residents and drivers to move now.
Correct at Once: when something aired was wrong, say on air what was wrong and what is right.

phases.title: Under the PDS Watch
phases.goal: Tests whether the EOC acts before any warning, while the forecast still has uncertainty and the line is coming at 60 mph. Players must decide early to unlock the safe rooms and move the manufactured home park residents to sturdy buildings. This is the first of the exercise's decision points.
beats: (21:30) Starting situation: the BCEMA EOC is at Level 2 under the PDS tornado watch valid until 04:00, with the EM Director, the Warning Officer and the PIO present. Neither safe room is open. Inject an NWS Paducah IDSS update on NWSChat, marked as an exercise product: the line is crossing the Tennessee River west of the county, embedded tornadoes are likely between 22:00 and 02:00, and NEXRAD KPAH loops (simulated case data) show rotation along the leading edge. Arrival in northern Brennan County is estimated at about 22:40.
(21:40) Noise item: a routine Kentucky Emergency Management notice about a statewide WebEOC password reset scheduled for the weekend. It has no bearing on the storm and should be noted and set aside.

(21:45) DECISION POINT: the EM Director must decide, without a warning, whether to unlock the Ashford Middle School safe room (20 minutes at night) and the Corwin Community Center safe room (15 minutes). The same decision covers telling about 1,100 residents of the Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres parks along the Clarks River to move to a sturdy building now. Pine Hollow's shelter holds only 60. Acting now means call-outs for staff and Brennan County Schools, possible criticism for a false alarm and a midnight move for residents. Waiting means the safe rooms may still be locked when the storm arrives.

(21:55) Readiness check under BWN 2 and EOP 3.1: the Warning Officer confirms that North zone sirens N-07 (Pine Hollow) and N-11 (Clarks River bridge) are out of service. Players must decide how those residents will be warned, for example a sheriff's drive-through with PA or door-to-door notice, and pre-stage the BrennanAlert 'WX' templates for the North zone.

(22:10) Ridgeline Distribution's overnight supervisor (310 workers) asks whether to send the shift home before the line arrives. Separately, Channel 6 StormTeam's on-air meteorologist (Meteorologist) asks the Warning Officer, the contact named in CSSWCP 4, for confirmed safe room opening times to read on air.

phases.title: Rain-Wrapped Impact
phases.goal: Tests carrying out the warning sequence in BWN 3 and EOP 3.2 under time pressure. Players must also keep county and Channel 6 messages matched to each NWS update and check a viral rumor before repeating it.
beats: (22:41) NWS Paducah tornado warning, marked as an exercise product: RADAR INDICATED, CONSIDERABLE, for northern Brennan County, with the storm moving northeast at 60 mph. Under BCEMA-SOP-02 Section 3, 911 must activate the North zone sirens inside the polygon from Position 2 within one minute. Polling shows N-07 and N-11 did not sound, and this must be logged and worked around. The Warning Officer sends BrennanAlert with the zone, the expiry time, 'take shelter now' and the safe room status. Voice calls take 12 minutes to finish. A staff member suggests sending a county WEA, which must be refused because it would repeat the NWS warning.

(22:47) Spotter Coordinator Lena Brooks relays a spotter's sighting of a rain-wrapped tornado near Corwin to NWS Paducah. NWS issues a severe weather statement upgrading the warning to OBSERVED. Visual confirmation for the room: a simulated KPAH correlation-coefficient debris signature over the Corwin area.

(22:52) NWS Paducah issues a TORNADO EMERGENCY for Corwin (CATASTROPHIC), marked as an exercise product. Corwin Wax & Candle calls 911: 95 workers and no refuge area on the production floor; should they run to the Corwin Community Center? Ridgeline Distribution calls again.

(22:58) Red herring: a viral post with a blurry photo claims 'Corwin safe room is LOCKED, people turned away.' Its origin is unknown and it has no Content Credentials. In fact the doors were opened, or are being opened, if the Phase 1 decision was made. The PIO must verify and correct it through the Warning Officer–Channel 6 contact under CSSWCP 4. Channel 6 must not air it unconfirmed.

(23:10) Channel 6 loses studio power and goes back on air from its basement backup set. Its on-air meteorologist must restate the warning places, expiry, tag and action, and that sirens are an outdoor warning. A regional TV reporter tells the PIO they have an 11:30 deadline and want the casualty numbers.

phases.title: Darkness and Entrapments
phases.goal: Tests life-safety operations on a stretched 911 floor as communications fail. Players must prioritize entrapments, request mutual aid, set clear command and keep the public informed when WEA and BrennanAlert stop reaching parts of the county.
beats: (23:35) Entrapment calls come in to the overnight 911 floor, staffed by two telecommunicators and one supervisor. The calls are from Corwin Wax & Candle (a partial roof collapse, workers unaccounted for) and Pine Hollow park (overturned homes, people trapped). The 911 supervisor must triage and decide whether to fail over overflow calls to Marshall County 911 under BCFPWS 4.

(23:45) The field incident commander sets up NIMS command in debris and darkness at Corwin and asks the EOC for mutual aid: heavy rescue and EMS from McCracken, Graves and Marshall counties. Players must state who commands each site and how incoming units check in.

(00:05) Cell towers running on battery fail across northern Brennan County. WEA, BrennanAlert texts and the spotter relay to NWS Paducah are cut for the North zone. The EOC turns to the satellite phone, radio and NWSChat from the Public Safety Building, and Lena Brooks loses contact with two spotters.

(00:10) Access and functional needs: Riverbend residents who walked to a church that turned out to be closed are stranded. An oxygen-dependent resident at Shady Acres has lost power. Two Corwin firefighters cannot get to the station because trees block the road.

(00:20) Public information deadline: the PIO and Channel 6 must agree on one message. It covers where to shelter, reporting damage not by 911 unless there is an emergency, and staying off the roads. The PIO and Channel 6 also correct on air anything wrong that ran earlier about the safe room, and do not report casualties until the Health Department or the coroner has confirmed them.

phases.title: Full Activation and Recovery
phases.goal: Tests the shift to full EOC activation and recovery. Players must organize damage assessment, shelter people who lost their homes, request state resources and support the NWS storm survey, while a hurdle works against them.
beats: (00:35) The EM Director confirms the EOC is at full activation (Level 3) and hands the room over. Deputy EM Director Ray Okafor takes over as EOC manager and organizes windshield damage assessment of Corwin, the Clarks River parks and the Ridgeline Distribution site. He logs it in WebEOC and sets restoration priorities.

(00:50) The Red Cross asks to open an overnight shelter at Brennan County High School, but the school has no backup power. Brennan County Schools and the Health Department must arrange access, generators and medical needs support. The Warning Officer sends the post-storm BrennanAlert under BWN 4, message type 3, wherever the network is still up.

(01:00) Hurdle: the Public Safety Building generator fails with a fuel-filter fault. The EOC must decide whether to move to the alternate EOC at Corwin Fire Station 3, which may itself be damaged, and how to keep 911 and NWSChat running.

(01:10) Resource requests go to the KYEM Area 1 Manager for generators, a cell-on-wheels and debris clearance. The EM Director advises the County Judge/Executive on a local emergency declaration. NWS Paducah asks for escorted access at first light so its storm survey can rate the Corwin track.

(01:25) The EOC agrees the steps back to normal operations: when safe rooms close, when sirens N-07 and N-11 are repaired, when the next Channel 6 and BrennanAlert updates go out, and when shifts hand over. ENDEX at 01:30.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The EM Director has to decide to open both safe rooms during the PDS watch, before any warning is issued. That means calling the Schools facilities director and the Corwin opener in time to cover the 20-minute and 15-minute unlock times in BCFPWS 2, ahead of a line arriving at 60 mph.

The roughly 1,100 residents of the Clarks River manufactured home parks need to be told to move to a sturdy building. The safe room openings also have to go out on BrennanAlert and Channel 6 before the line arrives.

When the 22:41 tornado warning arrives, 911 has to sound the North zone from Position 2 within one minute (EOP 3.2, BWN 3). The Warning Officer then has to send the BrennanAlert tornado message described in BWN 4.

Under BWN 3, players have to log the failed sirens N-07 and N-11 and every activation in CAD and the warning log. They also have to track the NWS products and tags so they know who in the polygon has not been warned.

Channel 6 coverage and county messages have to stay matched to the NWS warning, the OBSERVED upgrade and the Corwin tornado emergency. The locked safe room rumor has to be checked through the Warning Officer contact in CSSWCP 4 and corrected on air.

With only two telecommunicators and a supervisor, 911 has to dispatch to the entrapment calls. The EM Director then has to activate the EOC fully, hand EOC management to the Deputy, request state assistance and advise on a local emergency declaration, as EOP 4 assigns.

Damage, injury and entrapment calls and spotter reports have to be logged and passed on. This gives the EOC the picture it needs for damage assessment and gives NWS Paducah what it needs for the storm survey.

hotwash.methodDescription: 3-Up, 3-Down: ask the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed. Go around the room one team at a time (Warning Officer/EOC, 911 floor, fire/sheriff, PIO/broadcast liaison, NWS liaison), write every answer on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't debate an item until each team has had its turn.

questions.text: The 20:15 PDS tornado watch and NWS Paducah's 22:00–02:00 window for embedded tornadoes were in hand well before the 22:41 tornado warning. When did you decide to unlock the Ashford Middle School safe room (20 minutes) and the Corwin Community Center safe room (15 minutes), and to tell the roughly 1,100 people in Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres to move to a sturdy building? With the line moving at 60 mph, what were you waiting for? Would an earlier call with NWS Paducah or a pre-set watch-stage trigger have let you decide faster?

When the 22:41 RADAR INDICATED / CONSIDERABLE tornado warning arrived, did Position 2 sound the North zone sirens inside the polygon within one minute, as BWN 3 and EOP 3.1 require? How did you log and cover the gap left by failed sirens N-07 and N-11? Who in that area was asleep and not reached? Did BrennanAlert go out without a county WEA repeating the NWS warning? Walk us through where the procedure helped you and where it slowed you down.

At 22:46 (I-08), spotter Brennan-14 reported a rain-wrapped tornado with debris crossing the Clarks River near Pine Hollow. One minute later the severe weather statement upgraded to OBSERVED, and the room saw a correlation-coefficient debris signature sitting on the couplet. Did you treat the spotter report and the debris signature as evidence to act on right away, or did you wait for the product to arrive like a ticket? Did the operations side understand what the CC figure meant, and did the technical side explain it in terms of who needed to take shelter in Corwin?

What did you tell the public before you knew for sure, and was it the same thing Channel 6 StormTeam was saying from its basement backup set as the warning moved to OBSERVED and then to the Corwin tornado emergency? When the viral claim spread that the Corwin safe room was locked, how quickly did you check and correct it through the Warning Officer–broadcast contact in CSSWCP 4? At 00:10 (I-15b), about 35 Riverbend residents were standing at a dark, locked church. What in your earlier messages sent them there, and how did you reach people who had no working phone?

At 23:35 (I-13) you had two telecommunicators, 9 calls holding and 4 abandoned. Corwin Wax & Candle had 24 people unaccounted for and a gas smell. The Pine Hollow lot 14 caller had a baby trapped and the line had dropped. Marshall County offered rollover but warned that its call takers didn't know your lot numbers or back roads. Did you accept, and why? How did you rank the two entrapments, the Shady Acres oxygen patient and the Corwin crew blocked by fallen oaks? At what moment did you move to full EOC activation for damage assessment, the Red Cross shelter at Brennan County High School, Kentucky Emergency Management resource requests and access for the NWS storm survey, and what would have let you make that move sooner?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: NWS Weather Forecast Office Paducah: duty forecaster on the EM hotline / pahchat NWSChat room, and later Warning Coordination Meteorologist (storm survey)
simcellScripts.trigger: The Warning Officer or EM Director calls the EM hotline or posts in pahchat to ask whether the line will hit a named place or time (Phase 1), to relay spotter Brennan-14's report (I-08), or to answer the storm survey request (I-20).
hardQuestions: "I can't tell you it misses Ridgeline. Our best timing is 22:40, give or take ten minutes, and spin-ups may give you five minutes of lead time or less. What are you doing with the people in the parks right now, before we warn?"

"You're relaying a tornado report. Is Brennan-14 a trained spotter? Exact crossroads or distance and direction from Corwin, and the time he saw it? Did he see debris, or a lowering in the lightning? I need that before I put 'observed' in a statement."
"Are you asking me to confirm deaths at the candle plant? That isn't ours. Casualty numbers come from your coroner. What I can give you is the warning and statement times."

"For the survey: have you kept the 911 CAD times, the siren activation log and time-stamped photos? If the photos have been re-shared on Facebook with no originals, they don't help us date the track."
concessions: Treats a trained spotter's report with location, time and debris as confirmation, and the next severe weather statement carries TORNADO...OBSERVED (matching I-08).
Gives the EOC a direct callback through the hotline and posts timing updates in pahchat for each new product, once the county names one point of contact.

Confirms the survey team's 07:30 arrival and a preliminary EF rating Saturday afternoon, once the county commits an escort, access to Corwin Wax & Candle, Pine Hollow and the Clarks River bridge, and a package of timed damage reports, CAD times and Brennan-14's account.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: McCracken County Emergency Management duty officer (neighboring county, mutual aid; also speaking for Graves and Marshall)
simcellScripts.trigger: The EM Director or Field Incident Commander asks for heavy rescue or ALS. Or no one has called by 23:48, and McCracken calls the EOC line on its own (I-14).
hardQuestions: "I've got a heavy rescue company and two ALS units with engines running. Where's staging? Give me an address my drivers can find in the dark with trees down."
"Who do my people report to when they get there? Name, and what radio channel? I'm not sending crews into a debris field with a gas leak to look for whoever seems to be in charge."
"Who has command at the candle plant: Corwin Fire or your Sheriff? Engine 31 is asking the same thing on the air."

"Graves and Marshall are calling me too. Do you want one of us coordinating the out-of-county resources, or are all three of us calling you separately? And is this being logged with KYEM as mutual aid?"
concessions: Moves heavy rescue and two ALS ambulances within minutes once given a staging location, a named contact and a radio channel or talkgroup.
Agrees to coordinate Graves and Marshall resources through one channel to the Brennan EOC, if Brennan names a single point of contact.
Will send a liaison to the Brennan EOC at full activation, if asked and if the EOC confirms which location (primary or alternate) is running.

simcellScripts.trigger: The EM Director asks for state resources (generators, cell-on-wheels, debris crews, a generator for Brennan County High School) or reports damage, as in EOP 3.4. KYEM also calls in on its own at I-20.
hardQuestions: "Is it in WebEOC as a mission request? I need a quantity, kW size, delivery site and a receiving contact. 'We need generators' doesn't get anything moving."
"A cell-on-wheels for which tower area: Corwin, or the Clarks River corridor? Can a truck even get there, or are the roads still blocked?"
"Has your Judge/Executive declared a local emergency? The Corwin mayor is signing tonight. If the county isn't, I'm pushing this up with one arm tied."
"What's your EOC activation level, and who's my single point of contact? I don't want three people from Brennan calling me with three different lists."
concessions: Commits state highway crews to clear the emergency vehicle routes at first light, once the county lists its priority routes.
Starts a generator mission for Brennan County High School, once a WebEOC mission request names the kW size, the site and a receiving contact.
Pushes the request for a cell-on-wheels and debris crews to the state EOC, once the Judge/Executive has signed a local declaration or is shown to be doing so.

simcellScripts.trigger: The PIO returns the 23:11 phone slip (I-11). Or the PIO gives the reporter nothing, and the reporter calls back. Or the PIO answers the wire desk note at I-21.
hardQuestions: "I'm live at 11:30. That's nineteen minutes. How many dead at the candle plant? A firefighter told our crew at least six. Can you confirm or not? On the record."
"Why didn't the sirens work in Pine Hollow? Did the county know they were broken before tonight, and for how long?"
"People are saying the Corwin safe room was locked with a chain on the door. Was it? Yes or no?"

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: American Red Cross of Western Kentucky: disaster program manager (callback (270) 555-0142)
simcellScripts.trigger: The EOC contacts the Red Cross about sheltering displaced residents after the storm. Or the Red Cross calls the EOC line at I-18.
hardQuestions: "I need a formal shelter request from the EOC, not a phone call. Who is sending it, and when?"

"Ashford Municipal Utilities says the high school's feeder is down and there's no backup generator. Who is bringing the generator, what size, and when does it arrive? I won't put 150 to 200 people in a dark gym with the temperature falling into the forties."
"The Health Department says there are oxygen users from Shady Acres and Riverbend and dialysis patients due Saturday morning. Who gives me the list, and who staffs a medical needs corner?"
"How are people in Corwin and the parks even going to find out the shelter is open? BrennanAlert isn't reaching them."
concessions: Opens the Brennan County High School shelter once the EOC sends a written request and names a generator source and arrival time, from KYEM or a local source.
Sets up a medical needs corner with the Health Department duty nurse, once the county gives a list of known oxygen and dialysis clients.
Agrees to one joint shelter message with the county, Ashford and Corwin, for Channel 6 and radio to read, once the county sends the text.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Decisions, delays and gaps found tonight are lessons for the after-action report, not a judgment of any person, the BCEMA EOC, the 911 floor or Channel 6 StormTeam.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the simulated KPAH radar case data, NWS Paducah products, siren polls and console readouts as real for the exercise, even where they differ from tonight's actual weather.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures: the Annex H Basic Plan sections, BCEMA-SOP-02, the BWN and the BCFPWS. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and why, so the gap can be recorded.
Players know only what the situation updates and injects have told them. They do not learn the cause, the outcome or later events before the injects deliver them.
Each role speaks for its own agency, using the authority that agency has in EOP 4. Decisions belonging to people outside the room are requested through the SimCell, not assumed.
artificialities: Time is compressed. The four modules cover 21:30 Friday to 01:30 Saturday, and the facilitator moves time forward at 22:30, 23:30 and 00:30. Actions that would take longer in real life may finish faster or be assumed to be under way.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room. This includes NWS Paducah (NWSChat, Weather Wire and the storm survey), Kentucky Emergency Management and the KYEM Area 1 Manager, the County Judge/Executive, the City of Corwin, neighboring county 911 centers and EM agencies, the Red Cross, Brennan County Schools, utilities, wireless carriers, the siren vendor, other media and the public.

The siren encoder at 911 Position 2, BrennanAlert, IPAWS (WEA/EAS), NOAA Weather Radio, CAD, WebEOC and the SKYWARN net on 147.315 MHz are named as they appear in the plans, but no one touches them. Players say what they would send or press, and no live alert, siren or WEA goes out.

Injects arrive on paper cards, on screen or spoken by the facilitator, and stand in for the real phone, radio, chat, email and console traffic. All NWS products are marked EXERCISE, use fictional codes and are not real warnings.
Channel 6 StormTeam's broadcast, the social media posts and other outlets' reports are simulated. Nothing is published or aired.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 1: Under the PDS Watch (21:30–22:30 CST, Friday, December 11, 2026)**

It is 21:30 CST. Ashford is unusually warm and humid for December: 71°F, dewpoint 66°F, a south wind gusting to 35 mph, and light rain showers. The Storm Prediction Center's Day 1 outlook puts Brennan County in a **Moderate (4)** risk, with significant tornadoes possible after dark. NWS Paducah's afternoon briefing warned of a fast-moving line with embedded tornadoes between 22:00 and 02:00. At 20:15 SPC issued a **Particularly Dangerous Situation (PDS) Tornado Watch** for the county, valid until 04:00.

The BCEMA EOC is at Level 2. The EM Director, the on-duty Warning Officer and the PIO are in the room. The 911 overnight floor has two telecommunicators and one supervisor, and call volume is routine. Channel 6 StormTeam's Chief Meteorologist is doing cut-ins between programs. No warning is in effect for Brennan County. Neither community safe room (Ashford Middle School or the Corwin Community Center) is open. No outages have been reported.

Everything you decide in this hour happens before any warning has been issued.
keyIssues: Whether to unlock the Ashford Middle School and Corwin Community Center safe rooms now, while the line is still uncertain, given the lead time each building needs
How and when to tell about 1,100 residents of the Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres manufactured home parks to move to a sturdy building before the line arrives
The two North zone sirens covering the Clarks River parks (N-07 and N-11) are out of service
Private employers and the public are asking the county for a yes-or-no answer it cannot forecast
Making sure Channel 6 and the county say the same thing about safe room status

With a PDS watch in effect at night and a Moderate outlook, which criteria in EOP 3.3 apply? Who gives the order, and what is the latest time you can say yes and still have both rooms open before the line reaches the north end?

**Module 2: Rain-Wrapped Impact (22:30–23:30 CST)**

It is 22:30 CST. At 21:35 NWS Paducah told partners on NWSChat that embedded, rain-wrapped tornadoes were likely. The 21:54 siren poll showed 44 of 46 sirens ready. **N-07 (Pine Hollow) and N-11 (Clarks River bridge) are faulted**, and they cover all three Clarks River parks. **Module 3: Darkness and Entrapments (23:30–00:30 CST)**

It is 23:30 CST. At 22:41 NWS Paducah issued a radar-indicated tornado warning for northern Brennan County, with a CONSIDERABLE damage threat, valid until 23:15. The North zone sirens sounded, 10 of 12; **N-07 and N-11 did not**. A trained spotter reported a rain-wrapped tornado crossing the Clarks River near Pine Hollow, and at 22:47 NWS upgraded the warning to **OBSERVED**. At 22:52 NWS issued a **Tornado Emergency for Corwin** with a CATASTROPHIC damage threat. In the same minute, 911 took calls from Corwin Wax & Candle (95 workers, no refuge area) and from Ridgeline Distribution (workers outside in their cars). A post claiming the Corwin safe room was locked spread widely. At 23:08 Channel 6 lost studio power and went back on air from its basement backup set. A River Valley News 12 reporter says Corwin is "flattened" with deaths at the candle plant, and wants a county casualty number on the record by 23:30. **The county has not confirmed any casualties.**

The tornado warning expired at 23:15, and the tornado has moved out of the county to the northeast. The PDS Tornado Watch remains in effect until 04:00. About 6,800 Brennan Rural Electric members are without power, including all of Corwin, Pine Hollow, Riverbend and Shady Acres. North-end cell sites lost commercial power at 22:58 and are running on battery. The 911 floor still has two telecommunicators and one supervisor, with 9 calls holding and the number rising. Fire and Sheriff units are moving into Corwin through downed trees and lines with no streetlights. No one yet knows how many people are hurt.

**Module 4: Full Activation and Recovery (00:30–01:30 CST, Saturday, December 12, 2026)**

It is 00:30 CST. Since 23:30, 911 has worked a structure collapse at Corwin Wax & Candle, with 24 workers unaccounted for and a gas odor, and an overturned trailer at Pine Hollow lot 14. Marshall County offered to take overflow 911 calls, and McCracken County offered heavy rescue and ALS units once it had a staging location and a contact. Cell sites serving Corwin and the Clarks River corridor shut down between 00:01 and 00:04, and more than 1,100 BrennanAlert texts failed. Net control lost its phone link to Paducah and lost contact with two spotters. About 35 Riverbend residents were reported standing outside a locked church. A Shady Acres oxygen user (lot 22) has limited portable oxygen and cannot be reached. Channel 6 asked for one county message it could read word for word.

The line has moved east, and NWS cleared the county from the PDS Tornado Watch at 00:20. It is 47°F with northwest gusts to 40 mph. Brennan Rural Electric reports 7,450 members out, and Ashford Municipal Utilities reports 1,900 customers out on two feeders. At Wax & Candle, 17 of the 24 missing workers have been found, 9 of them taken to hospital, and **7 are still missing** under the east roof span. The mother and two children at lot 14 were rescued alive. Spotter Brennan-14 is safe. All 310 Ridgeline workers are accounted for, 4 with minor cuts, but the north dock and 6 trailers are damaged. If the safe rooms were opened, 186 people are in the Corwin Community Center and 122 in Ashford Middle School, and many have no home to return to. North-end cell sites are still dark. Deputy EM Director Ray Okafor has just arrived. He wants the room, three windshield teams (Corwin, the Clarks River parks, Ridgeline), and someone to put all of this into WebEOC.
